scenes.headline: How a video model paints a game, chunk by chunk
scenes.sub: Code keeps the world. A rough proxy goes in. Video comes out.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Riffle! A program sketches a game world, and a video model paints it, one short chunk at a time.

scenes.text: Each chunk of video sees the proxy up to now and nothing after it, so the proxy can come from a program that is still running.
scenes.say: Each chunk sees the sketch up to now, and nothing after it. So the sketch can come from a game that is still running.

steps.say: Right, its proxy. Depth, and a class for every pixel.

scenes.title: One chunk, from code to pixels

steps.say: The program keeps the world state, and compiles each moment into a proxy.
The video model reads a start image, a caption, and the proxy up to this chunk. Never the next one.
In four steps it paints seventeen frames, about seven tenths of a second.
Those frames go into a cache. The next chunk looks back at the last five.

scenes.title: Who each chunk may look at

steps.label: The original: one window, all at once
steps.say: The original model painted a five second window at once. Every frame could see the future.

steps.label: Streaming: nothing from later chunks
steps.say: The streaming version masks that away.

steps.label: And only a short span
steps.note: positions restart at the span; cached keys are rotated back
steps.say: And keeps a short span. Positions restart at the span, so they stay where the model was trained.

scenes.title: Teaching it not to trust its past
scenes.say: Its own past is slightly wrong, so training teaches caution.

items.say: Every chunk gets its own noise level, so history is never clean.

items.text: Roll out on its own output
items.say: A fast student streams many chunks on its own output.
A teacher says where it should go, a critic tracks where it goes.
The result paints a chunk in four steps.

scenes.label: to render 0.708 s of video on one H200
scenes.note: 7.2x slower than real time, before decoding
scenes.say: The catch. Each chunk takes five point one seconds on one big GPU, for seven tenths of a second of video.

scenes.text: Causality makes a live proxy possible. The renderer still has to get about seven times faster.
